reason: Verified in the source and by driving the page. states.day in render-b.js (lines 316-328) emits exactly five text nodes plus foot(); the rendered field contains ten elements at both 390 and 1440, three of which are the footer, and there is a 124px dead band between the closing line and the rule at every width. The quoted copy is exact. Worse than the seat says: the state's own chrome label reads 'SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER, MORNING' while the body asserts 'Everything on the plan has happened' — but the fixture's last live milestone, 'Wedding day' 2026-10-03, is that morning and has not happened, so the surface contradicts its own data. The footer also reads 'UPDATED 15 JULY 2026' on the wedding morning, eleven weeks stale, which no other state has to carry. Nothing in interaction-check.mjs asserts anything about this state beyond the generic 'states today' check at line 242, so this is not a restatement of a gate, and no constraint is at risk: the fix is composition and copy, no fourth colour, no third weight. One claim in the finding is wrong and I discount it — states.print renders horizon() plus behindBlock() plus measure(), not the day composition, so print does not echo this screen. The core claim stands regardless. The fix as written is NOT buildable: it asks for --px-per-hour over 'the running order of 3 October' and names 'Next · 12.40 · Cars to the church', but fixture.js is date-only (milestones carry date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', no time field, no running order), and the brief's binding rule is 'Never placeholder text, never a hand-rolled imitation of the data'. Inventing a wedding-morning schedule is exactly that. Confirmed with a sharpened fix that stays inside the data on hand.
sharpenedFix: Do not invent hours. Give the day state the day by running the existing machinery at a day-of clock. In render-b.js, parametrise ahead(), behind() and the daysTo call sites with a clock argument defaulting to F.today, and render states.day with clock = F.project.primaryDate.date so the arithmetic is the fixture's own days() accessor and cannot disagree with any other surface. Then: (1) keep the masthead as it is — 'Today', the names, the long date — but let the count grammar arrive rather than vanish, so the number the whole product has been counting down reads its final value on the one morning it matters, using the existing .b-count / .b-num / .b-unit; (2) below the indigo rule, name what is actually happening from the fixture instead of denying it — the milestone dated 3 October is 'Wedding day', and the fixture already ships the verbatim label for it in STATE_LABEL.now, 'Happening now' (vocabulary.ts); (3) fill the 124px dead band with behindBlock() at the day-of clock, which is the eight real dated milestones from 'We said yes' on 2 January to 'Venue walk-through' on 19 September plus the one not going ahead — that is the keepsake reading, it is the same object the print sheet already uses, and it needs no data that does not exist; (4) reword the closing line so it belongs to the evening and to a plan that has been kept, not to an emptied counter, and hold it for after the day's own milestone has passed. Leave the foot's 'Updated 15 July 2026' alone or suppress the updated stamp on this state only — an eleven-week-old timestamp under a wedding morning reads as an abandoned page. In interaction-check.mjs assert what is checkable against date-only data: that the day state names its own date and the title of the milestone dated that day; that its count is F.days(primaryDate, primaryDate) rather than a hardcoded string; that behind-row order and dates match the fixture at the day-of clock; and that no line on the surface claims nothing is left while a live milestone is dated today. Reshoot the state at 390/768/1280/1440.
